$about: 2026-08-06, later the same day: the two severe documentation-honesty findings re-run against the current tree before anything was written. DOC-16 closes - both halves measured, and the earlier round's disproving numbers turned out to be an artifact of the same ambiguous command. DOC-10 stays open on purpose: the gap is now recorded and gated forward, and twelve entries were deliberately not reconstructed. Neither observation carries a `fix` field, deliberately: the render counts those as merged pull requests, and the change this round rests on is open and unmergeable while GitHub Actions is in a major outage. The evidence names the commits instead, which is checkable today.

observations.evidence: Re-run against the showcase working copy at ~/git/repository-standards-showcase, head 770f2fc. The outcome blocks now read 4 / 3 / 3 (May scheduling-core, June notifications, July invoicing). Measured over the full boundary days - `git log --oneline --since="<opened> 00:00:00" --until="<closed> 23:59:59"` - real history returns exactly 4 / 3 / 3, and the commits are nameable rather than counted: 4915a07 82cc8a7 7436938 4cad89b for May, fb6ce9f 62bd50c a93c3ba for June, 99fc7a2 aeba459 cda4110 for July. Two halves had to move for that to be true, and only one of them is in this repo. The numbers were corrected in the showcase's own history by c80e6f7 (2026-08-05), one day after the 2026-08-04 observation. What stayed broken until this change is the prescription: cycle-close named the command with bare dates, and git resolves a bare --since/--until date as an approxidate - that date at the moment the command runs. The same command over the same history therefore returns 3 / 2 / 1 at 19:24, 3 / 2 / 2 at 00:00 and 2 / 1 / 1 at 12:00, and it can include both the cycle-open and cycle-close commits only when the open commit's time of day is later than the close commit's. That last figure is the finding: the 2 / 1 / 1 the 2026-08-04 round recorded as the real numbers was itself a time-of-day artifact of the unqualified command, not a stable measurement - a disconfirmed claim on the disproving side, published here for the same reason the claiming side's are. The number was also published wrong twice before it was right: 63 / 51 / 88 originally, then 9 / 6 / 3 in 9fdfe52 (2026-08-02) under the explicit claim that those were what git log returns, then 4 / 3 / 3. cycle-close now writes the times out and specs/work-cycles records why the window is the two boundary days whole. Two caveats the record should carry rather than the reader discover. First, the history these windows are measured over was authored, not accumulated: 19 of the showcase's 34 commits carry a whole-minute timestamp with author and committer date identical, and they are exactly the 19 oldest - everything up to and including the first commit-count correction on 2026-08-02, which covers all three cycles. The commits are real git objects and the counts over them are real, but their dates were chosen when the demo was built, which is also why the boundary commits cluster at a morning open and an evening close and why the ambiguity bit as hard as it did. The 15 newer commits carry second-level times. Second, the target slug: this observation keeps the case+target key its predecessors used so that it supersedes them, and the tree actually measured is the showcase working copy named above.

Both halves re-run against the current tree of this repo (repository-standards/core, branch off de58256) before anything was changed. The script half is closed and was closed before this round: `scripts/changelog.mjs` exists nowhere in the checkout, and docs/method/changelog-process.md no longer promises it - it now says 'No script ships for this, deliberately' and explains what went out with the per-PR fragments folder. Nothing else in the tree claims the script ships: `grep -rn changelog.mjs` returns only historical changelog entries and this suite's own case text and run evidence. The entries half still fails, and the case fails with it. `grep -nE '^## \[?1\.0\.' CHANGELOG.md` returns exactly two headings, 1.0.13 and 1.0.0. Reading `git log -p -- VERSION` rather than assuming the range: thirteen commits moved VERSION between those two releases - to 1.1.0, 1.1.1, then 1.0.2 through 1.0.12, all on 2026-08-03 - so the range the case was written with is wrong in two ways. VERSION never held 1.0.1 (63f5bc0 walked 1.1.1 back and wrote 1.0.2 directly, because R25 as first written matched its own trigger and promoted two ordinary PRs), and 1.1.0 / 1.1.1 did exist and were never named. The unrecorded span is 07ad235..4b1179d, 32 commits; `git log --oneline 07ad235..4b1179d -- CHANGELOG.md` returns one commit, a285218, which only rewrote an organization name inside older entries. So no entry was written for any of it. Two checks against the obvious objection that this history was re-authored and lost entries it once had: none of the 32 commits carries a whole-minute timestamp (32 of 32 are second-level), the signature that would suggest supplied dates, and the release note cut with 1.0.13 says the same thing contemporaneously - 'this changelog has no entries between 1.0.0 and 1.0.12'. The gap is what the record says it is, only mis-counted. The case's given and procedure were corrected to derive the version list from git instead of assuming a contiguous 1.0.1-1.0.12 range.
observations.waiver: Left open deliberately, with the gap recorded rather than filled. What shipped: a dated section in CHANGELOG.md stating exactly which versions have no entry, that VERSION never held 1.0.1, the 32-commit range to read, and the correction to the 1.0.13 note's 'twelve version bumps'; plus a mechanical check in tools/tree-check.mjs that fails when VERSION names a version with no matching `## <version>` heading, so the omission cannot repeat silently. What did not ship, and will not: twelve reconstructed entries. Twelve of the thirteen bumps are one commit each and could be transcribed from their subjects, but 1.1.0 arrived twenty commits after 1.0.0 and splitting those nineteen unversioned commits across release headings would be a guess presented as a record, in the file whose only value is being checkable. The case asks for an entry at every historical version; that is still not true, so this stays fail rather than being redefined into a pass.
